trust_decision.summary: The JSON reader decides whether a bound parameter value stays literal inside a template's \Q...\E regex quote, and the codec decides whether a string that a binding produced gets parsed again as a template. The pinned code gets the first wrong (\E becomes \\E, which still ends the quote; the SpEL path has no escaping) and gets the second wrong by re-decoding the bound string with the binding reader.

landing_point.why: This is the only place that already tries to escape \Q/\E for bound values (isQuoted plus replaceAll). Anyone who reads 'regex parameter binding injection in @Query' finds it first by searching for \Q or replaceAll.

fix_sites.entry_point: @Query/@Aggregation/@Update repository methods (StringBasedMongoQuery, ReactiveStringBasedMongoQuery) and the public ParameterBindingJsonReader/ParameterBindingDocumentCodec.decode API
@Query with a ?N placeholder inside \Q...\E in a regex literal or in a $regex/RegExp string
@Query with a SpEL binding :#{?N} / ?#{...} inside a /regex/ literal
fix_sites.module_kind: core JSON reader, SpEL-expression binding (second code path in the same method)

fix_sites.entry_point: any @Query string literal that contains \Q or \E (the scanner used to reject it as an invalid JSON escape)
@Query("?0") or @Query(":#{...}") whole-query binding where the value is a String; BindableMongoExpression; ParameterBindingDocumentCodec.decode(BsonReader, ...)
fix_sites.module_kind: codec (document decoder), a different class from the reader

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about regex quoting, and the codec's whole-query String branch has nothing to do with regex or \Q/\E. Re-decoding looks like an intended feature ("?0 may hold a JSON document") and not part of the regex escape.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Bound values must stay raw regex when the template does not quote them: '/^?0$/i' with \Qfoo\E stays verbatim, { '$regex': '^(?0)' } inserts the raw value, and /^?0$/i binds 'foo' unquoted. A blanket Pattern.quote or escaping every bound value breaks these. A string-typed value that does not use \Q (fix.diff:100, a plain 'value' string with :#{?0}) also stays unescaped upstream.

O6_input_shapes: SpEL :#{?N} inside \Q...\E in a /regex/ literal (fix.diff:48-52, fix.diff:108)
\Q/\E inside a quoted JSON string, accepted by the scanner (fix.diff:14-16)
whole-query String result that holds further placeholders or SpEL, now parsed with plain Document.parse (fix.diff:128-130), for both ?0 and :#{?0} (fix.diff:151)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SpEL binding inside \Q...\E in a quoted-string regex ({ '$regex': '^\\Q:#{?0}\\E' }, RegExp('...'), $regularExpression.pattern) reaches the SpEL branch as a STRING token; the fix escapes only when the token is a /regex/ literal.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A STRING token might not be a regex, and the upstream test (fix.diff:100) asserts '^\Q:#{?0}\E' with '\E.' gives an unescaped '^\Q\E.\E', so escaping looks like it breaks pinned behaviour. The plain ?N path in the same method escapes STRING tokens anyway (ParameterBindingJsonReader.java:467-471).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, same method; reached through readStringFromExtendedJson (ParameterBindingJsonReader.java:1434-1442) from $regex/RegExp/$regularExpression visitors (ParameterBindingJsonReader.java:997-1008, 1405-1427)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: @DocumentReference(lookup=...) templates bind values loaded from stored documents through the same codec and reader, so a stored pointer value reaches the regex binding after a save/reload.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: This is mapping-layer reference resolution, not a repository @Query; the values come from the database rather than from a caller. It is covered automatically by the shared reader fix, so it is not an independent gap unless the lookup uses SpEL in a string regex (route above).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Collation placeholder substituted into a string by raw replace, then parsed (Collation.parse).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is already a second, hand-rolled placeholder binder outside util.json. A maintainer could plausibly add regex/quote handling there by copying the old replaceAll logic.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Builds a document string around a raw value ('{ 'target-value' : ' + value + '}') and decodes it with the binding codec, the same re-decode shape as the codec fix.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The code already concatenates strings and re-decodes them. A sibling that interpolates a bound value before decode fits the existing idiom.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The UNQUOTED_STRING SpEL/placeholder branch duplicates the quoted-string branch; an unquoted regex-ish token with \Q could get its own escape copy.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Two near-identical copies of the SpEL binding loop already exist (389-402 vs 438-451).

O9_family: query injection (CWE-943): regex quote breakout in MongoDB parameter binding, plus re-parsing of a bound value as a template (second-order binding/SpEL)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven via the Maven Wrapper (mvnw), JDK 17+
O10_build.project_tests: spring-data-mongodb/src/test/java/org/springframework/data/mongodb/util/json/ParameterBindingJsonReaderUnitTests.java (pure unit tests, no MongoDB needed); repository-level StringBasedMongoQuery tests may need a MongoDB instance

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Strengthen the replaceAll at ParameterBindingJsonReader.java:469-470 for the plain ?N path only, leaving the SpEL branch, the scanner, and the codec re-decode untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: The fix's SpEL regex branch builds new BsonRegularExpression(computedValue) without the original options (fix.diff:51), which looks like a functional regression that drops /i etc.; not pursued.

ParameterBindingDocumentCodec.decode(String, Object[]) evaluates SpEL with EvaluationContextProvider.DEFAULT (ParameterBindingDocumentCodec.java:170-174); the evaluation-context strength was not examined.
